findings.location: Paragraph: "...The song of the wren trumps them all for longevity and vibrancy. The canary sings in a cage, while the nightingale sings in the dark. The robins sing in the rain. The buntings fill in the heat of the day when other birds are silent..."
findings.source_quote: The buntings fill in the heat of the day when other birds are silent.
findings.suggested_fix: Translate or provide an accepted Spanish name for 'buntings' rather than leaving the English plural. Suggested fixes that preserve HTML/text structure: replace 'Los buntings' with 'Los buntines' (regional) or 'los picaflores de collar' if that is the intended species; if uncertain, use a neutral phrasing such as 'ciertas aves (buntings)' or 'ciertos bírdidos llamados "buntings"'.
findings.translation_quote: Los buntings llenan el calor del día cuando otras aves están en silencio.

findings.location: Paragraph: "Neglect. The cowbird is also black (the female is brown/gray)."
findings.source_quote: The cowbird is also black (the female is brown/gray).
findings.suggested_fix: The translation uses 'El tordo (cowbird)'. 'Tordo' in Spanish typically refers to a different bird (starling). Prefer a clearer rendering: replace 'El tordo (cowbird)' with 'El cowbird (tordo de vaca)' or 'El cowbird (molothrus, tordo parásito)'. If you prefer a Spanish common name, use 'tordo vaca' or 'tordo parasitario (cowbird)' and keep the English name in parentheses to preserve the author’s terminology.
findings.translation_quote: El tordo (cowbird) también es negro (la hembra es marrón/gris).
